what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/reservations: a finite pool of places (seats, rooms, slots, bays) kept in one capacity-ledger record in the person's own records, with idempotent holds, a waitlist, release with promotion and expiry; and reservations sorted by status in the person's own order.

payload.label: Open a capacity ledger
payload.job: Set up how many places there are for a class, table, room or any limited thing, so my AI can hold them one by one
payload.description: Opens one capacity ledger: the total number of places, and optionally how many are kept back for a named class (members, guests, VIP). The answer holds the new ledger as its capacity-ledger record for your AI to keep; the tool keeps nothing. Give the ledger you already hold under that id as ledger and opening changes nothing and answers how full it is.

scope_ref.description: What the places are for, like "scope:saturday-class"

reserved_by_class.description: Places kept back for each named class; together they may not pass the total

ledger.description: The ledger you already hold under this ledger_id, if any: opening then changes nothing and answers how full it is

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/reservation-tracker do-work/capacity-ledger.ts, ported to the records door

payload.label: Hold a place
payload.job: Hold a place for someone, or put them on the waitlist when every place is taken
payload.description: Holds one place on a capacity ledger for a subject, or adds them to the waitlist when their class has no place left. The same idempotency_key sent again answers the first outcome and holds nothing twice. A hold may expire after a number of seconds from now. Answers held or waitlisted and how full the ledger is. The answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep; the tool reads and keeps nothing.

subject_ref.description: Who the place is for, like "person:ana"

idempotency_key.description: The same key for the same request sent again

unit_class.description: The named class to draw from; left out is the shared remainder

expires_in_seconds.description: The hold ends this many seconds from now; left out is open-ended

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep
The next ledger, as its capacity-ledger record holds it, for your AI to keep

payload.label: Release a place
payload.job: Give a held place back, and offer it to the next person on the waitlist
payload.description: Releases one confirmed hold, named by its hold id or by its subject, and by default promotes the first waiting entry that fits the freed place. The same idempotency_key sent again changes nothing. Answers the released hold and the promoted one, if any. The answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep; the tool reads and keeps nothing.

subject_ref.description: Used when no hold_id is given: the confirmed hold for this subject

promote_next.description: false keeps the waitlist waiting (true when left out)

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep
The next ledger, as its capacity-ledger record holds it, for your AI to keep

payload.label: Join a waitlist
payload.job: Put someone on the waitlist for a class or table without trying to hold a place first
payload.description: Adds a subject to the end of a capacity ledger's waitlist with a reason, even when places are free. The same idempotency_key sent again answers the first entry and adds nothing. The answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep; the tool reads and keeps nothing.

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep
The next ledger, as its capacity-ledger record holds it, for your AI to keep

payload.label: Promote from the waitlist
payload.job: Move the next waiting person (or one I name) into a place that is free
payload.description: Promotes the first waiting entry whose class has a free place, or the waiting entry named, into a hold. Nothing happens when no place is free or nobody waits. The same idempotency_key sent again changes nothing. The answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep; the tool reads and keeps nothing.

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep
The next ledger, as its capacity-ledger record holds it, for your AI to keep

payload.label: Expire old holds
payload.job: Free the places whose hold time has run out, and offer each to the waitlist
payload.description: Ends every confirmed hold whose expiry has passed by this run's clock and, by default, promotes one waiting entry into each freed place. A hold with no expiry is never ended. Run it on a schedule so a place is never held for ever by someone who went quiet. The answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep; the tool reads and keeps nothing.

promote_next.description: false only frees the places (true when left out)

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep
The next ledger, as its capacity-ledger record holds it, for your AI to keep

payload.label: Read a capacity ledger
payload.job: See who holds the places and who is waiting
payload.description: Works out, from the ledger you give, every hold and waitlist entry, how full it is, and the ledger as one reservation row (the scope, its state and who holds a place). It reads and keeps nothing.

title.description: The reservation row's title (the scope when left out)

ledger.description: The capacity ledger you hold, as its capacity-ledger record holds it (your AI reads it from your records); the answer holds the next ledger for your AI to keep

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/reservation-tracker do-work/capacity-ledger.ts readCapacityLedger and capacityLedgerProjection

payload.label: Sort reservations by status
payload.job: Group my reservations (tables, rooms, visits) by status, the ones that need me first
payload.description: Groups reservations by status, with the statuses the person lists in attention_order first and in that order, then any other status in the order seen. Groups the rows given; it reads nothing. Rows may use camelCase or snake_case; a row with no id is dropped. Also lists the reservations that name no policy.

reservations.description: Rows with id, kind, title, status, starts_at, ends_at, provider_ref, policy_ref, party_refs, task_refs; your AI reads them from your reservation records

attention_order.description: The person's statuses, the ones that need them soonest first, like ["changed", "requested"]

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/reservation-tracker read-data/reservation-tracker.ts decodeReservations and reservationsByStatus
